arguments.content:
In the United States, cancer survival rates have improved significantly over recent decades. The five-year relative survival rate for all cancers combined rose from 48.9% in 1975-1977 to 69.2% in 2007-2013, reflecting advances in early detection and treatment.

Most deadly cancers (by mortality):
Lung cancer (5-year survival: ~20%)
Colorectal cancer (5-year survival: ~65%)
Pancreatic cancer (5-year survival: ~13%)
Brain cancer (5-year survival: ~36%)
Leukemia (5-year survival: ~30%)

Uncommon cancers (by cases per year in the U.S., ascending):
Mesothelioma (~2,000 cases/year)
Testicular cancer (~10,000 cases/year)
Uterine cancer (~50,000 cases/year)
Kaposi sarcoma (~5,000 cases/year)
Malignant melanoma (~10,000 cases/year)
